newsitem.title: USA: FBI became aware of Chinese allegations in 1995.
newsitem.headline: FBI became aware of Chinese allegations in 1995.

text.p: The FBI became aware in 1995 of possible Chinese plans involving efforts to influence Congress and gave the information to the CIA and the State Department, the Justice Department said on Monday.

But it denied Republican Sen. Orrin Hatch's account that the FBI had warned key elements of the Clinton administration and some congressional officials in 1995 of an alleged Chinese plan to use laundered funds to influence U.S. elections.
"The FBI provided copies of an internal FBI cable on this matter to staff-level offices at the CIA and the State Department," the Justice Department said of the FBI's actions in 1995.

"As is often the case with cables designated for 'routine' transmission, the Justice Department did not receive a copy at that time. Nor is there evidence that the cable was provided to the White House or the House and Senate Intelligence Committees," it said.

Hatch, a Senate Intelligence Committee member from Utah, said Sunday on the CBS program "Face the Nation" that FBI warnings went to the State Department, CIA, Justice Department, two Congressional committees and as many as seven lawmakers.

The Justice Department said the 1995 cable did not mention any members of Congress by name nor did it contain information regarding any plans by China to influence the U.S. government's executive branch.

It said in a three-paragraph statement that the FBI did not provide any briefing about the contents of the cable until May 1996, "after it acquired additional information." The FBI then told White House National Security Council aides about the allegations.

President Clinton complained last week that he and his senior staff were never told about the allegations because of restrictions placed on passing the information to higher-ups by the two FBI agents. The FBI contradicted Clinton in a rare public dispute.

Attorney General Janet Reno said last week a "misunderstanding" between the FBI and White House National Security Council aides was to blame for the information not reaching Clinton, and she ordered a review of the procedures involved.
